transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Time: 16:00 UTC (48 minutes)
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CitrineAI CTO), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Daniel Park (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand CitrineAI's plan to move from OpenAI managed endpoints to either Redwood Dedicated or Private. They also run an internal vLLM/TGI stack for latency-sensitive workloads. Primary concerns: eval parity vs OpenAI, migration effort, latency & cost tradeoffs, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and runbook for running benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- Current stack & usage patterns
- Performance expectations and SLOs
- Eval parity and model compatibility (tokenization, function-calls, embeddings)
- Dedicated sizing, autoscale, and burst capacity
- Security & compliance (SAML/SSO, SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Migration plan and next steps

Action items (also in metadata above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Blake, AE on the account, with Maya Chen our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alex (CitrineAI): Good, thanks. Busy week but good to chat.
[00:09] Priya: Hi, yes thanks. We wanted to run through options for moving a chunk of our traffic off OpenAI into either Redwood Dedicated or Private.
[00:15] Maya (Redwood): Great, can you give a quick overview of current usage? volumes, models, and which parts are most latency sensitive?
[00:22] Priya: Sure. Roughly 2M tokens/day currently to OpenAI across chat prompts and embeddings. The embeddings are mostly for semantic search, about 20% of tokens. The rest is chat. We also run an in-house vLLM/TGI cluster for low-latency routing for our conversational assistants, that's maybe 15% of requests but it's very latency-critical.
[00:38] Daniel (CitrineAI): And practically we want predictable unit cost — OpenAI has been fine but the tail spend and new pricing plans are a concern. Also we need more control over data residency and audit logs.
[00:48] Jordan: Makes sense. Two immediate paths: Redwood Hosted API for quick lift-and-shift with token-level pricing, or Dedicated pools if you want predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale, and data isolation. Private if you need VPC/on-prem. What's your security posture requirement? SOC2? SSO?
[01:05] Priya: We are SOC2 in process, SAML SSO is required for dev access, and KMS integration for embeddings at rest would be ideal. Also we need audit logging for requests.
[01:14] Maya: All supported. Dedicated/Private options integrate with customer KMS/HSM and provide audit logs per request, plus RBAC. Our console surfaces token-level cost and latency.
[01:24] Alex: Two technical questions early on: 1) Will model outputs be identical to OpenAI? And 2) how much prompt rework do we need — tokenization differences, function-calling, etc.
[01:33] Maya: Short answer: parity depends. If you're using OpenAI proprietary models, exact parity for behavior will vary; Redwood curates open models and verified performance profiles. For general LLM behavior we can match at the model-family level but exact token-for-token may differ. For function-calling we support similar structured outputs, but you'll want to run evals. Also tokenization differences can slightly change token counts, which affects cost.
[01:52] Priya: We have a suite of eval prompts — a couple thousand prompts used to track regressions. We'll need to run those against your dedicated infra to confirm parity.
[01:58] Jordan: Totally — that's standard. We usually run your eval set on a Dedicated pilot and compare metrics (accuracy, latency, hallucination rate). We'll propose a benchmark plan.
[02:07] Daniel: On the infra side, what's the Dedicated autoscaling model look like? We have spiky traffic.
[02:12] Maya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscale policies and burst capacity. You can pin GPU types, set min/max nodes, and define routing policies (latency-first or cost-first). In spikes we can burst to hosted capacity as a fallback — good for graceful degradation.
[02:24] Alex: About vLLM/TGI: we currently run TGI for some models because it reduces cold-start latency. If we move to Dedicated, will we lose those optimizations?
[02:33] Maya: Our runtime incorporates many of the same optimizations — continuous batching, KV cache management, optimized kernels for different architectures — so cold-starts and steady-state latency should be comparable. For absolute micro-optimizations folks sometimes keep a small vLLM edge pool for the most latency-critical paths, while routing bulk traffic to Dedicated for cost reasons.
[02:50] Priya: Any differences in embeddings between providers? We use OpenAI embeddings for semantic search; swapping models changed results before.
[02:57] Maya: Embedding vector distributions differ by model. Redwood can host validated embedding models, and we recommend running an embedding parity eval (cosine similarity on a sample set). We can also provide recommendations on quantization and model variants that keep parity while lowering cost.
[03:12] Alex: How do we do gradual rollouts? We don't want to flip a switch.
[03:17] Jordan: We support canary deploys and A/B routing, with automatic fallback to a hosted variant if error rates or latency thresholds breach. You can pin session-level routing as well.
[03:27] Daniel: On the security front: will the control plane see request payloads in Dedicated? We need to be sure customer data doesn't leave their VPC for Private, and for Dedicated we need guarantees too.
[03:36] Maya: For Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed — no customer data leaves their VPC. For Dedicated, customer data is logically isolated and encrypted at rest, and we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS. Audit logs are available and can be shipped to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 docs and architecture diagram.
[03:52] Priya: Great. A practical question: how long to get up and running for a Dedicated pilot?
[03:57] Jordan: Usually 2–4 weeks for initial sizing and provisioning, quicker if you accept standard sizing. Benchmarks take 1–2 weeks depending on scope.
[04:06] Alex: Cost — can you ballpark monthly run cost for our 2M tokens/day?
[04:10] Jordan: We need to see token mix and sequence lengths but rough back-of-envelope: hosted cost is higher per token; Dedicated with committed capacity usually reduces unit cost by 30–50% at volumes like yours. We'll send a pricing worksheet.
[04:21] Priya: One big migration worry is prompt engineering drift. We've tuned many system prompts for OpenAI models. Will those continue to behave?
[04:29] Maya: Some re-tuning is common. That's why we prioritize running your eval set and a small canary to measure drift. We can also set regression alerts tied to those eval sets in Redwood Optimize.
[04:41] Alex: Are there any known incompatibilities with TGI/vLLM saved checkpoints or model formats?
[04:46] Maya: We support major model formats (PyTorch, GGML in some cases) but custom TGI forks or very custom checkpoints can need conversion. We'll take a look at your models. Often it's straightforward but we should validate during the pilot.
[04:58] Daniel: From an infra POV, we also care about observability — per-route latency, token-level cost, and traceability for a user session across calls.
[05:06] Maya: Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, and tracing hooks you can integrate with your observability stack. You can export logs or we can ship to a customer-managed log sink.
[05:18] Jordan: Ok recap and proposed next steps — we'll: 1) send pricing and Dedicated sizing worksheet, 2) Maya will share a benchmark plan and migration checklist for vLLM/TGI, 3) Citrine to share eval prompts and token distributions, 4) schedule a technical deep dive next week.
[05:36] Priya: Sounds good. For the benchmark, we want to measure latency P95, throughput, and an accuracy/hallucination metric on our eval set.
[05:45] Maya: We'll include those metrics in the plan. Also will propose quantization profiles and candidate model variants to test.
[05:52] Alex: Any blockers on our side to get pilot rolling?
[05:55] Jordan: Just the eval set, token stats, and sign-off on the pilot SOW. We'll draft the SOW after we send pricing.
[06:02] Priya: We'll aim to get you the eval set and token hist by Friday (2026-04-10).
[06:07] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links to SOC2, the benchmark plan, and the pricing worksheet.
[06:15] Alex: Thanks. Looking forward to the tech deep dive.
[06:18] (call ends)
